parsed_items.source_span: Inside a cell there are many different parts, and each part has its own job to do. These parts are called organelles.
Three important parts found inside cells are: - The cell membrane... - The nucleus... - The cytoplasm... - The mitochondria.
This is the thin outer layer that surrounds the cell. Its job is to protect the cell and to control what substances are allowed to enter or leave.
The nucleus... contains the instructions that direct everything the cell does.
This is the jelly-like substance that fills the inside of the cell. The other organelles float inside the cytoplasm.
These organelles are sometimes called the "powerhouse" of the cell, because their job is to produce the energy the cell needs to function.
But there is one important difference: plant cells have an extra layer outside the cell membrane called the "cell wall".
The cell wall is rigid and gives the plant cell a fixed shape and extra protection, which is one reason plants can grow tall and stand upright.
A living organism's whole body is built from cells. Groups of similar cells work together to form tissues, tissues form organs, and organs form body systems.
This is true for both plants and animals — from the smallest insect to the largest tree, every part of a living organism's body is ultimately made of cells.
